According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On newsletter, Apple is preparing to include up to 1.5TB of RAM in its upcoming M7 Ultra chip. When that happens, Apple Silicon will finally catch up to the maximum RAM configuration offered by the top-of-the-line 2019 Intel Mac Pro.

RAM capacity has always been a limitation of Apple Silicon Macs, mainly because Apple solders the RAM directly onto the same chip as the processor — a design that delivers extremely high transfer speeds and is what makes unified memory possible. But of course, it also means RAM capacity is constrained by the size of the chipset itself.

However, according to Mark Gurman, Apple finally appears ready to close that gap. The company is preparing an M7 Ultra chip configuration with 1.5TB of RAM:

He also noted that due to the ongoing chip shortage, the 1.5TB RAM configuration may not actually make it to market. Even so, Apple has engineered the M7 Ultra to support that capacity.

Earlier this year, Apple discontinued the 512GB configuration of the M3 Ultra Mac Studio, followed by the 256GB version, leaving 96GB as the only option for the top-end Mac Studio. Switching to the M4 Max, on the other hand, allows configurations of up to 128GB.

Apple will also introduce an all-new M5 Ultra chip later this year, featuring up to 768GB of unified memory — setting a new record for Apple Silicon.

At Apple's current RAM pricing (roughly an extra $25 for each additional 1GB), upgrading from the base 128GB configuration to 1.5TB of RAM would likely cost more than $35,000.
